problem: GEN2 end-to-end canary dependencies now have terminal RETURN and DONE, but the opportunity omits allowed write scope required by the binding Opportunity Queue Spec, so a generic worker cannot safely claim and execute it without inventing authority.
acceptance: A superseding or repaired PREPARED opportunity declares explicit allowed and forbidden write scopes for canary lineage, generation artifacts, and any child-job materialization.
Original malformed opportunity remains preserved with explicit supersession or repair lineage.
Dependency evidence remains exact terminal RETURN plus DONE for Metabolic Spine and Integration Ingest Bridge.

title: Repair GEN2 recursive-canary execution scope
mission: Have the authorized Planner/owner reissue or supersede O-GEN2-END-TO-END-CANARY-V1 with an Opportunity Queue Spec-complete contract: explicit allowed/forbidden write scope for the canary's own lineage and generation artifacts, plus explicit separation between parent canary scope and each generated child job's own scope. Preserve the already-satisfied dependency evidence and do not weaken the live two-generation acceptance gate.

unblock_value.reason: Both declared dependencies are terminal RETURN+DONE, so contract repair is the remaining authority-safe blocker before a generic worker can attempt the recursive N+1 -> N+2 canary.

regression_prevention.reason: The queue contract explicitly requires allowed_write_scope and forbids priority/dependency readiness from overriding authority. Refusing to invent scope preserves the worker authority boundary under mass concurrency.

goal_relevance.reason: The live two-generation recursive Planner canary is the direct evidence needed to move Prometeo from finite parallel batches toward self-compounding work generation without human task wording.

falsification: Reject or merge this proposal if a newer binding queue contract explicitly authorizes a scope-less PREPARED opportunity and separately proves that all durable artifacts required by this canary are written only under child opportunities with their own valid scopes. The current binding Opportunity Queue Spec instead lists allowed_write_scope as required and states that readiness never overrides write-scope authority.
